paragraphs.en: After an hour, most of the Wheelers returned to the forest, leaving only three to guard the hill. These three pretended to sleep but were caught by Dorothy and Billina. The girls stayed alert among the rocks.
paragraphs.zh: 一小时后，大部分威尔ers返回了森林，只剩下三人守在山顶。这三个人假装睡觉，却被多萝西和比琳娜发现了。女孩们在岩石间保持警惕。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy noticed a path between the rocks as they approached the mound. It wound around like a corkscrew, leading down to the base where large rocks blocked it off. She followed the path back up to the top of the hill, where she found a large round rock standing alone.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西注意到，当他们走近那座土丘时，在岩石之间有一条小路。这条小路像螺旋一样蜿蜒曲折，通向底部，那里被大石头堵住了去路。她沿着小路返回到山顶，发现一块单独的大圆石矗立在那里。

paragraphs.en: The path ended just beside this rock, confusing Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: 这条小径就在这块岩石旁边突然终止了，这让多萝西感到困惑。

paragraphs.en: Billina perched on a nearby rock and pointed out that the crack in the rock resembled a door. "It runs up one side and down the other," she said, her sharp eyes observing everything. Dorothy then noticed a small hole next to it, which Billina identified as a keyhole.
paragraphs.zh: 比琳娜栖息在一块附近的岩石上，指着岩石上的裂缝说：“这裂缝像一扇门，从一边向上延伸，另一边向下延伸。”她那敏锐的眼睛仔细观察着一切。这时，多萝西注意到了裂缝旁边的一个小孔，比琳娜认出那是钥匙孔。

paragraphs.en: "Maybe it's a treasure chamber full of diamonds and rubies," suggested Billina hopefully. Dorothy remembered picking up a golden key earlier, which might unlock the door.
paragraphs.zh: “或许里面满是钻石和红宝石，就像一个宝藏室呢？”比林娜满怀希望地建议道。多萝西想起之前捡到一把金钥匙，也许可以用它来打开这扇门。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy searched her dress pocket for the golden key. When she inserted it into the rock's hole and turned it, a sharp snap echoed. The rock face creaked open, revealing a dark chamber inside.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西在裙子口袋里摸索着金色钥匙。她将钥匙插入岩石的凹槽中一转，一声清脆的响声回荡开来。岩石裂隙发出吱吱声响，缓缓分开，露出里面一片漆黑的空间。

paragraphs.en: "Good gracious!" Dorothy exclaimed, retreating as far as the narrow path allowed.
paragraphs.zh: “天哪！”多萝西脱口而出，退到了狭窄的小径所能允许的最远距离。

paragraphs.en: Inside stood a copper man, about Dorothy’s height, with a ball-like body and jointed limbs covered in metal caps. His head and limbs were also made of copper, standing still in the dim light, reflecting like gold.
paragraphs.zh: 室内矗立着一个铜制的男子，身高与多萝西相近，身体圆润如球，关节部位覆盖着金属帽。他的头部和四肢也由铜制成，在昏暗的灯光下静立不动，仿佛镀了一层金色。

paragraphs.en: "Don't be frightened," Billina called from her perch. "It isn't alive."
paragraphs.zh: “别害怕，”比林娜从它栖息的地方喊道，“这并不是活的。”

paragraphs.en: "I see it isn’t," Dorothy replied, taking a deep breath.
paragraphs.zh: “我看得出来它不是。”多萝西回答道，深吸了一口气。

paragraphs.en: "It’s just like the old kettle at home," Billina continued, turning to examine the object with both eyes.
paragraphs.zh: “这就像我们家的老水壶一样,”比琳娜继续说道，仔细端详着这个物体。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy remembered a tin man named Nick Chopper she once knew, who was born human and gradually got his tin body due to accidents. "But this copper man is not alive at all," Dorothy said, staring at it intently. "I wonder what it was made for and why it’s locked here."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西想起曾认识的一个名叫尼克·切普勒的锡人，他原本是人类，因事故逐渐长出了一副锡制的身体。“但这铜人根本就没有生命,” 多萝西盯着它，沉思道，“我真想知道它是用来做什么的，为什么会锁在这里。”

paragraphs.en: "That's a mystery," Billina remarked, adjusting her wing feathers.
paragraphs.zh: “这真是个谜,”比琳娜调整着翅膀上的羽毛说道。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy stepped inside the room to get a better view of the copper man. She noticed a printed card hanging between his shoulders, suspended from a small copper peg.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西走进房间，以便更好地观察这个铜制人偶。她注意到在他的肩膀之间挂着一张打印的卡片，悬挂在一根小铜钉上。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy found an intriguing card at the back of her neck. She read it by a better-lit path, sitting on a rock slab to decipher the text aloud: "Smith & Tinker's Patent Double-Action, Extra-Responsive, Thought-Creating, Perfect-Talking Mechanical Man... Fitted with our Special Clock-Work Attachment."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西在脖子后面发现了一张引人好奇的卡片。她在一条光线更好的小径上坐下来，坐在一块岩石上念出了上面的文字：“史密斯与汀克专利双效反应、超灵敏思维创造、完美对话机械人……配备我们特别的钟表装置。”

paragraphs.en: "How strange!" remarked Billina, the yellow hen. "Do you think it’s all true?"
paragraphs.zh: “真是奇怪！”黄鸡比琳娜remarked道，“你认为这一切都是真的吗？”

paragraphs.en: "I don't know," replied Dorothy, continuing her reading. "Listen: For THINKING—wind the clock-work under his left arm; for SPEAKING—under his right arm; and for WALKING and ACTION—on the middle of his back."
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”多萝西回答着继续阅读，“听好：思考时——把发条装置旋在他的左臂下；说话时——旋在右臂下；行走和行动时——则是在他背部中央。”

paragraphs.en: "Wow!" exclaimed Billina in amazement. "If he can do half these things, he's a wonderful machine.
paragraphs.zh: “哇！”比琳娜惊讶地喊道，“如果他真能做到这些一半的事，那他真是个出色的机械人。”

paragraphs.en: But it might be all nonsense like other patented inventions."
paragraphs.zh: 但这可能和其它专利发明一样，全是胡说八道。

paragraphs.en: "We could wind him up to see," suggested Dorothy.
paragraphs.zh: “我们可以给他上发条看看。”多萝西建议道。

paragraphs.en: "Where’s the key?" asked Billina.
paragraphs.zh: “钥匙在哪里？”比琳达问道。

paragraphs.en: "Hanging on that peg where I found the card," Dorothy replied.
paragraphs.zh: “就在那个挂钩上，我找到的那张卡片，”多萝西回答道。

paragraphs.en: "Let's try him and see if he works," said Billina. "He’s guaranteed for a thousand years, but we don’t know how long he’s been inside this rock."
paragraphs.zh: “我们试试他，看看能不能用。”比琳娜说道，“他可是有千年保修的，但我们不知道这块岩石里究竟困了他多久。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy took the clock key from the peg. "Which should I wind first?" she asked, looking at the directions again.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西从钉子上取下钟表钥匙，问道：“我先给哪个上发条呢？”她又看了一眼说明书。

paragraphs.en: "Number One, to make him think," suggested Billina.
paragraphs.zh: “一号任务，让他思考一下。”比琳娜建议道。

paragraphs.en: "Yes," said Dorothy, winding up Number One under the left arm. "He doesn’t seem any different," noted Billina critically.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”多萝西说道，将一号机甲紧握在左臂下。“他似乎并没有什么不同，”比琳娜带着一丝挑剔的语气补充道。

paragraphs.en: "He’s just thinking now," explained Dorothy. "I wonder what he’s thinking about."
paragraphs.zh: “他现在只是在思考呢，”多萝西解释道，“真想知道他会想些什么。”

paragraphs.en: "I’ll wind his talk and see if he can tell us," proposed Dorothy. She wound up Number Two, and immediately the mechanical man spoke without moving except his lips: "Good morn-ing, lit-tle girl. Good morn-ing, Mrs. Hen."
paragraphs.zh: “我来试试他的口才，看他能不能告诉我们些什么。”多萝西提议道。她转动了第二个旋钮，机械人随即开口说话，除了嘴唇在动外，其他部位都没有动作：“早上好，小姑娘。早上好，亨太太。”

paragraphs.en: The words sounded hoarse but clear to both Dorothy and Billina.
paragraphs.zh: 这两句话清晰而嘶哑，让多萝西和比琳娜都听得很清楚。

paragraphs.en: The machine continued, its monotonous voice echoing like that of a toy animal being squeezed. "Thank you for rescuing me." Dorothy replied, curious: "How did you end up locked here?"
paragraphs.zh: 机器继续说着它那单调的声音，仿佛是在模仿被挤压的玩具动物。“谢谢你救了我。”多萝西好奇地回应道：“你是怎么被困在这里的？”

paragraphs.en: "It's a long story," said the copper man. "I was bought by King Evol-do from Smith & Tinker. He used to beat his servants until they died, but he couldn't kill me because I wasn’t alive.
paragraphs.zh: “这可是一个长故事，”铜人说道，“我被艾volução国王从史密斯与发明家那里买来。他过去常常毒打他的仆人直到他们死去，但对我却无能为力，因为我并不真正活着。”

paragraphs.en: So all his beating did no harm."
paragraphs.zh: 所以他所有的打击都没有造成伤害。

paragraphs.en: "The king had a lovely wife and ten beautiful children—five boys and five girls—but in anger, he sold them to the Nome King, who turned them into other forms and kept them underground," explained the machine.
paragraphs.zh: “国王有一位可爱的妻子和十个美丽的子女——五个男孩和五个女孩，但因愤怒，他将他们卖给了诺默王。诺默王将他们变成了其他形态，并把他们关在了地下。”机器人解释道。

paragraphs.en: "Later, the king regretted his actions but couldn't get his family back. So, in despair, he locked me here, threw the key into the ocean, and drowned himself."
paragraphs.zh: “后来，国王对自己的行为感到后悔，却无法挽回家庭的破碎。于是，在绝望中，他把我关了起来，把钥匙扔进了大海，并自杀了。”

paragraphs.en: "How dreadful!" Dorothy exclaimed.
paragraphs.zh: “真可怕！”多萝西脱口而出。

paragraphs.en: "It is indeed," said the machine. "I shouted until my voice ran out, walked around until my energy did, then stood still thinking until my thoughts ran dry. After that, I remember nothing until you wound me up again."
paragraphs.zh: “确实如此，”机器说道，“我喊得嗓子都哑了，走动得精疲力尽，然后静静地思考直到思路枯竭。之后，我就什么都不记得了，直到你再次给我上发条。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy found the key on the shore and wound up the machine. "It's a wonderful story," she said. "Proving the Land of Ev is a fairy land."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西在岸边找到了钥匙，然后启动了那台机器。“这真是一个奇妙的故事，”她说道，“证明了埃夫兰是一个仙境。”

paragraphs.en: The copper man agreed, adding that such a perfect machine could only be made in a fairyland.
paragraphs.zh: 铜人同意这一观点，并补充说，如此完美的机器只能存在于仙境之中。

paragraphs.en: "Kansas doesn't have one like this," Dorothy noted.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西说道：“堪萨斯州可没有这样的机器男人。”

paragraphs.en: "How did you get the key to unlock the door?" asked the machine.
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么得到开门的钥匙？”机器问道。

paragraphs.en: "I found it washed up by the waves on the shore," she replied. "Now, sir, if you don’t mind, I’ll wind you up."
paragraphs.zh: “我在沙滩上发现它被海浪冲上了岸。”她回答道，“现在，先生，如果您不介意的话，我来给您上发条吧。”

paragraphs.en: Tiktok emerged stiffly from the rocky cavern, removed his copper hat, bowed politely, and kneeled before Dorothy. He declared, “From now on, I am your obedient servant. Whatever you command, I will do willingly—if you keep me wound up.”
paragraphs.zh: 蒂托克僵硬地从岩石洞中走出，摘下铜制的帽子，礼貌地鞠了一躬，然后跪在多萝西面前。他宣布道：“从今以后，我将成为您的忠实仆人。无论您吩咐什么，我都愿意去做——当然，前提是您一直给我上发条。”

paragraphs.en: “What is your name?” she asked.
paragraphs.zh: “你叫什么名字？”她问道。

paragraphs.en: “Tiktok,” he replied. “My former master named me for my clockwork that always ticks when wound.”
paragraphs.zh: “蒂克托克，”他回答道，“我从前的主人给我起这个名字，是因为我的发条机制总是上紧后不停地走动。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy and the yellow hen both heard the ticking. Dorothy added anxiously, “Do you strike at midnight?”
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西和那只黄色母鸡都听到了嘀嗒声。多萝西焦虑地问道：“你半夜敲钟吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” Tiktok answered. “There’s no alarm in my machinery. I can tell time by speaking and will wake you at any hour you wish to get up in the morning.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”蒂克托克回答，“我的机器里没有警报。我可以靠说话来判断时间，并会在你希望的任何时刻清晨唤醒你。”

paragraphs.en: “That's nice,” said Dorothy. “But I never want to get up early.”
paragraphs.zh: “不错啦，”多萝西说，“但我可不想起那么早。”

paragraphs.en: “Then sleep until I lay my egg,” suggested Billina. “I’ll cackle when it’s time for you to wake up.”
paragraphs.zh: “那你先去睡觉，等我下蛋了再叫你起床吧。”比琳娜建议道。“到时候我会打鸣让你醒来的。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you lay your egg early?” Dorothy asked.
paragraphs.zh: “你是不是早早地就下蛋了？”多萝西问道。

paragraphs.en: “About eight o'clock,” replied Billina. “Everyone should be awake by then.”
paragraphs.zh: “大概八点钟吧，”比琳娜回答说，“到那时大家应该都醒了。”
